# What This Means for Western North Carolina {#sec-conclusion}

```{r}
#| label: conclusion-numbers
#| include: false
drv <- py$shap_importance
dir_lr <- setNames(ifelse(py$lr_coefs$standardized_coefficient > 0, "raises", "lowers"), py$lr_coefs$feature)
best <- py$best_cv
plural <- function(verb) sub("s$", "", verb)   # "raises" -> "raise" for plural subjects

# Which feature groups clearly add value for the best cross-validated model
# (gain over the previous ladder row, interval above zero). group_label comes
# from the ladder-summary chunk in _modeling.qmd.
best_steps <- lad |> dplyr::filter(model == best$model, status == "evaluated", !is.na(pr_gain_vs_previous))
best_clear <- dplyr::filter(best_steps, pr_gain_vs_previous_lo > 0) |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(pr_gain_vs_previous))
best_unclear <- dplyr::filter(best_steps, pr_gain_vs_previous_lo <= 0)
group_gain <- function(row) sprintf("%s (%+.3f, interval %+.3f to %+.3f)", lc1(unname(group_label[row$rung])),
                                    row$pr_gain_vs_previous, row$pr_gain_vs_previous_lo, row$pr_gain_vs_previous_hi)
list_words <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) x else paste(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(x, 1))
headline_2 <- if (nrow(best_clear) == 0) "No feature group adds a reliable gain beyond season." else
  sprintf("%s adds the most beyond season.", unname(group_label[best_clear$rung[1]]))
```

::: {.lead-text}
Helene showed that in the mountains, one storm can outweigh a decade of ordinary ones. Carolina HighGround turns a decade of public records into a clearer picture of **where storms are most likely to become deadly or very costly, and why**, so that preparation can start before the next one.
:::

## Key findings

1. **Rare events dominate the toll.** In our `r length(p$study_counties)` study counties, a single week of `r p$highlight_event_name` accounts for `r scales::percent(story$hl_death_share, accuracy = 1)` of the storm deaths and `r scales::percent(story$hl_damage_share, accuracy = 1)` of the reported damage recorded from `r p$start_year` to `r p$end_year`. Planning around "typical" storms misses the ones that matter most.
2. **`r headline_2`** Our best cross-validated model (`r tolower(best$model)`, `r py$summary$n_features` features) reaches a PR-AUC of **`r fmt3(cv_best$pr_auc)` ± `r fmt3(cv_best$pr_auc_sd)`** (mean ± SD across folds), against a no-skill base rate of `r fmt3(cv_base)` and `r fmt3(season_row$pr_auc)` for a model that knows only the season. Groups whose added value is clear: `r if (nrow(best_clear) == 0) "none" else list_words(vapply(seq_len(nrow(best_clear)), function(k) group_gain(best_clear[k, ]), character(1)))`. On the `r p$validation_end_year + 1`-`r p$end_year` holdout, its top 10% of predicted risk holds `r ci_text(best$model, "top10_capture", fmt_pct)` of the high-consequence events, but `r fmt_pct(hs$share_test_positives_in_window[1])` of those events come from the `r p$highlight_event_name` week, so that number mostly reflects one storm.
3. **Developed places are not where the model puts the most risk.** In the logistic model, more paved surface `r dir_lr[["impervious_mean_250m"]]` predicted risk and steeper slopes `r plural(dir_lr[["slope_degrees"]])` it. One explanation is that urban flood reports are often minor while the worst events hit rural, steep places, but NOAA's reporting differs between urban and rural areas, so this pattern may partly reflect how events are recorded. We have not separated the two.
4. **Some groups we expected to matter add nothing measurable.** `r if (nrow(best_unclear) == 0) "Every group added a clear gain." else sprintf("For the %s, %s did not reliably improve predictions once the earlier groups were in the model. With only %s severe events in the development years, the data cannot detect small effects, so this means \"not shown\", not \"irrelevant\".", tolower(best$model), list_words(lc1(unname(group_label[best_unclear$rung]))), py$summary$devel_pos)`

## Who could use this

| Audience | How it helps |
|---|---|
| **County emergency managers** | Identify communities whose surroundings resemble past high-consequence events, and pre-position supplies (water, generators) before hurricane season |
| **NCDOT and local road agencies** | Prioritize inspection of crossings in steep, stream-dense, rural areas, where blocked roads cut off communities for weeks |
| **Schools and community organizations** | Plan continuity for places likely to lose power, water, and internet access for long periods, as our interviewees experienced |
| **Residents** | Understand that "hurricanes don't reach the mountains" is no longer a safe assumption |

## Next steps

```{r}
#| label: next-steps
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat(if (rain_used) {
  "* **Sharpen rainfall.** The model uses gridMET daily totals on a 4 km grid; hourly radar totals (e.g., Stage IV) would capture short, intense bursts.\n"
} else {
  "* **Add rainfall** (e.g., Stage IV radar totals) so the model can separate *how much rain fell* from *where it fell*.\n"
})
cat(if (svi_used) {
  "* **Go below the tract.** Tract-level CDC/ATSDR SVI is in the model; block-group or parcel data would show *who* within a tract is most exposed.\n"
} else {
  "* **Use tract-level vulnerability** (CDC/ATSDR SVI) instead of county averages, to see *who* within a county is most exposed.\n"
})
if (!rung_ok("+ Hydrology")) {
  cat("* **Measure upstream drainage** (flow accumulation, HAND) rather than point-and-buffer proximity.\n")
}
cat("* **Validate with local partners** in Buncombe and neighboring counties, and turn the interactive explorer into a planning tool.\n")
```
